title: A step toward: Petersen graph: some circuit with at most 6 AND gates, ORs free, is correct on its partial function with each variable bare in at… (step 1 of 2)
formal_statement: ∃ (x1 : Fin (6 : ℕ) → ℕ) (x2 : Fin (6 : ℕ) → ℕ) (x3 : Finset (Fin (6 : ℕ))),   (∀ (x4 : Fin (6 : ℕ)), x1 x4 < (2 : ℕ) ^ ((10 : ℕ) + ↑x4) ∧ x2 x4 < (2 : ℕ) ^ ((10 : ℕ) + ↑x4)) ∧     (∀ (x4 : Fin (10 : ℕ)), Fintype.card { x5 : Fin (6 : ℕ) // (x1 x5).testBit ↑x4 = Bool.true ∨ (x2 x5).testBit ↑x4 = Bool.true } ≤ (2 : ℕ)) ∧       have x4 : ℕ → ℕ := fun (x4 : ℕ) => List.foldl (fun (x5 : ℕ) (x6 : Fin (6 : ℕ)) => if x5 &&& x1 x6 ≠ (0 : ℕ) ∧ x5 &&& x2 x6 ≠ (0 : ℕ) then x5 ||| (2 : ℕ) ^ ((10 : ℕ) + ↑x6) else x5) (x4 % (1024 : ℕ)) (List.finRange (6 : ℕ));       have x5 : ℕ → Bool := fun (x5 : ℕ) => Decidable.decide (∃ x6 ∈ x3, (x4 x5).testBit ((10 : ℕ) + ↑x6) = Bool.true);       ∀ x6 ∈ [(50 : ℕ), (69 : ℕ), (104 : ℕ), (116 : ℕ), (138 : ℕ), (201 : ℕ), (208 : ℕ), (276 : ℕ), (385 : ℕ), (402 : ℕ), (521 : ℕ), (548 : ℕ), (554 : ℕ), (770 : ℕ), (773 : ℕ)], x5 x6 = Bool.false ∧ ∀ (x8 : Fin (10 : ℕ)), x6.testBit ↑x8 = Bool.false → x5 (x6 ||| (2 : ℕ) ^ ((0 : ℕ) + ↑x8)) = Bool.true
plain_statement: There are six pairs of numbers (L_i, R_i), each below 2^(10+i), and a set O of gate indices, such that each vertex v of the Petersen graph (edges 0-1 1-2 2-3 3-4 4-0 0-5 1-6 2-7 3-8 4-9 5-7 7-9 9-6 6-8 8-5) is bit v of L_i or R_i for at most two i, and the following evaluation is correct: put the input in bits 0-9; for i = 0 to 5 set bit 10+i when the word so far shares a bit with L_i and with R_i; output whether bit 10+i is set for some i in O. It outputs false at each maximal independent set of the graph and true when any one vertex outside it is added.

counterexample.description: Its literal negation pair, L-meta-8775, is checked (run-064875); recorded by the hub in the same act.
